whatItDoes: Shows current time for 4 default cities (NY/London/Tokyo/Sydney) and lets you add any IANA zone via select (Intl.supportedValuesOf or 20-zone fallback). Displays time via Intl.DateTimeFormat, updates every second, and shows diff vs local.
whyItExists: Remote teams need to see multiple zones and DST at a glance without installing a clock app. This does it with browser Intl APIs, no server, and live updates.
whoShouldUse: Distributed teams scheduling meetings, travelers checking destination time, and anyone comparing zones before a call.
useCases: Add Europe/Paris and America/Chicago to see Paris vs Chicago diff
Check if Tokyo is in DST today via the offset display
Use the live tick to time a meeting start across zones
instructions: View 4 default clocks updating every second. Pick a zone from the select to add a custom clock.
Each card shows local time, zone name, and offset/diff vs your local zone.
Remove any custom clock with the X button. All rendering is local via Intl.
examples: Input: Add Europe/Berlin → Output: Berlin 14:30 (UTC+2, +6h vs NY) live.
Input: Tokyo default → Output: Tokyo 21:30 JST (UTC+9) live tick.
bestPractices: Add only the zones you need — each adds a 1s interval
Use the diff to propose meeting times in the overlapping window
commonMistakes: Assuming the clock is server time — it is your device's clock formatted for that zone via Intl
Expecting historical DST — Intl uses current rules; past dates may differ if rules changed
faq: Is it uploaded? No — time is your device's Date formatted via Intl.DateTimeFormat in your browser.
Does it need a server? No — all zones are via Intl; no API call.
Can I add any zone? Yes — via supportedValuesOf if available, else a 20-zone fallback list.
